newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 1996/97 soybean crop 47 pct sold-Safras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 1996/97 soybean crop 47 pct sold-Safras.

text.p: Brazilian producers sold a record 47 percent of the 1996/97 soybean crop by the week ending March 20 compared with 32 percent at the same time last year, independent consultant Safras e Mercado said.

This was up from a five-year average of 30 percent and from the previous high of 40 percent during the same period of the 1993/94 harvest, Safras said in a weekly report. It noted that in view of a forecast bumper harvest of 27 million tonnes this year, the amount already negotiated was almost 13 million tonnes.

"Although part of these sales were based on the need for funds in order to meet costs, the greater part of trade was conducted to take advantage of the excellent quotations for soybeans on the Chicago bourse," Safras said.

The pattern of this year's anticipated sales showed that financing conditions still varied widely from region to region and growers were waiting to sell at prices between 10 to 20 percent above 1995/96 levels, Safras said.
It added that exporters had benefited from low international supply and the abolition of the ICMS export tax, which created fierce competition with crushers for soybeans on the internal market.
Forward sales, state by state, were as follows:
PARANA: A record 50 percent of the expected crop has already been sold, with the majority headed for export.

RIO GRANDE DO SUL: Although the 24 percent of advance sales represent a new record for the period, the state lags behind proportionally speaking. Sales for export but also for financing needs, since the drought in 1995/96 left farmers short of funds.
MATO GROSSO: Leads the pack with 65 percent of the crop sold, but a large proportion of this was done to fund planting.
MATO GROSSO DO SUL: Due to see a large injection of capital as a large proportion of sales were made in 1997 when prices were already rising.
GOIAS: Even though sales were initially aimed at funding planting, the state should see good economic recovery due to the high level of sales made after December.
